latitude.why: Open, debatable calls: exec the -e command directly vs typing into the shell; whether commanded launches adopt saved sessions; flag naming mirroring foot; hand-rolled parsing vs clap.

q1.position: `-e <cmd> [args...]`: everything after -e is the command argv, exec'd directly on the first pane's PTY via `tty::Options.shell` (like the TD_DEMO path), no shell wrapping; pane closes on exit.
q1.rationale: xdg-terminal-exec passes an argv vector after ExecArg; term.rs already sets options.shell for demos, and ChildExit already closes panes.

q2.position: `--app-id=<id>` (glued or space-separated) replaces the hard-coded "terminal-delight" in `WindowOptions.app_id` at `open_window`; no runtime `set_app_id` mutation needed.
q2.rationale: main.rs:17990 already plumbs app_id through WindowOptions; setting it once at creation satisfies the contract with zero gpui changes.

q3.position: `--working-directory=<dir>` feeds the existing seed path (same slot TD_SEED_CWD fills), landing in `PaneRestore.cwd` → `term::spawn_in(cwd)`; a vanished dir falls back gracefully as today.
q3.rationale: spawn_in already accepts cwd with dir-exists fallback; scratch_decision already seeds it — pure reuse, no new mechanism.

q4.position: `--title=<t>` overrides the computed `window_title()` result in `TitlebarOptions.title`; declared to consumers as `X-TerminalArgTitle=--title=` in packaging/terminal-delight.desktop.
q4.rationale: Title already flows through TitlebarOptions at open_window; the desktop key is how xdg-terminal-exec learns the flag.

q5.position: Add `X-TerminalArgExec=-e`, `X-TerminalArgAppId=--app-id=`, `X-TerminalArgTitle=--title=`, `X-TerminalArgDir=--working-directory=` to the desktop entry; keep existing Exec/Categories (TerminalEmulator already present).
q5.rationale: Mirrors Omarchy's shipped foot.desktop exactly, so xdg-terminal-exec composes argv identically; trailing `=` means glued values.

q6.position: Unchanged: a bare launch adopts via `instance::resolve_session()` — the most-recently-saved unheld session, restoring its layout — exactly today's behavior; `--help`/`--version`/unknown-flag replies stay as-is.
q6.rationale: The contract only adds flags; regressing default adopt/restore behavior would break every existing launcher and user habit.

q7.position: Hand-rolled: a new `parse_launch(argv) -> LaunchSpec` in app/src/main.rs, unit-tested, running after the subcommand dispatch and replacing `flag_reply`'s unknown-flag refusal for these four flags. No clap.
q7.rationale: Repo deliberately hand-rolls its tiny CLI (flag_reply, subcommand ifs); -e's consume-rest semantics is trivial; a crate adds nothing.

q8.position: Any contract flag (`-e`/`--app-id`/`--title`/`--working-directory`) forces the explicit-scratch path: no session adoption, no restore, no lock contention, no persistence — same as TD_SCRATCH/TD_SEED_* today. The seed carries the command.
q8.rationale: A commanded window is a throwaway like a torn-off pane; restoring a saved multi-pane layout around htop, or stealing a session lock, would be wrong.
